proposal.name: Run component checks and finish their evidence

issue_plan.name: Run component checks and finish their evidence
issue_plan.summary: Complete #244 in nine sequential plumbing changes: repair receipt literals, finish separate evidence records, discover Python and TypeScript components, execute checks through existing pinned tools, connect the explicit gate, and show each component in the dashboard. Proof, bounded or sampled conformance, executed tests/runtime assertions and declared assumptions stay separate; neighbors never inherit assurance. Each change updates SPEC.md and README.md, replacing stale #224 references while preserving legacy verification, model-only checking and ratified statements/locks. The merger records new evidence, identity and execution policies and reconciles D-0163, cited by the issue but absent from this checkout; builds cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Render explicit receipt literals as code elements
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish the explicit-receipt rendering fix requested by #244. internal/receipt/receipt.go already entity-escapes source-derived text, but statement names, toolchain values, bounds and other literals still pass through backtick spans, where entities display verbatim: No_Double becomes No_Double. Use escaped <code> elements consistently for literals in explicit receipts, including fingerprints, ratified statements, bounds and toolchain values. Escape values before assembling markup, without escaping twice. Preserve original JSON values and legacy Markdown.

Acceptance must check the rendered visible text for underscores, ampersands, angle brackets, backticks, pipes and line endings, including No_Double and toolchain image/tag values. Check that hostile text cannot create HTML, extra table cells/rows, links or forged proof statuses, and retain the existing component-table escaping tests.

Under D-0122 update SPEC.md and README.md for the fix; replace stale #224 references with #244's ratified plan, retaining current execution limits. Decisions: D-0013, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161 and the #234 attribution contract implemented by #242. The issue cites that contract as D-0163, but its journal entry is absent from this base: the merger must reconcile the record through the decision tooling and correct the stale claim that it is unrecorded, without inventing its contents. Keep pinned statements, locks and decisions/ unchanged.

issues.title: Record separate component evidence and all of its inputs
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Extend the explicit component evidence foundation in internal/project, internal/verify and internal/receipt for #244. Keep the existing exact-target proof contract and add independent conformance, runtime-check and trusted-assumption records. Conformance records name the selected driver/check, model, ratified bounds, sampled/bounded-exhaustive mode, observed counts and attempt coverage. Runtime evidence records selected tests and exercised assertions with actual runner outcomes, never inferred target coverage. Trusted assumptions are explicit target declarations with identity, statement, reason/origin and source snapshot, always assumed/unverified. They cannot prove code or satisfy executable checks. This does not introduce production instrumentation or infer assumptions from source.

Extend manifest configuration only as needed for explicit assumption declarations and reproducible check invocation metadata. Inventory/configuration remains intent, never successful evidence. Attribution requires canonical target/check IDs, matching input snapshots, runner/tool identity and actual outcomes. Missing, failed, timed-out, skipped or empty attempts must not yield successful evidence. Reject unknown, duplicate, unselected and stale references atomically. Updating one kind preserves other kinds and the gate outcome; reject changed inventories atomically if retained evidence would have stale snapshots. Proof requires successful exact-target coverage of all selected contracts; neighbors/helpers inherit nothing.

Add separate provenance for selected tests/drivers outside production scope: their files and all actual execution inputs must be hashed without adding them as production coverage rows. Fingerprints bind declarations, selections, model/bounds, all input hashes, evidence/outcomes and tool pins; canonical order, relocation and existing volatile exclusions remain. JSON/Markdown list all components and separate evidence kinds without scores or blanket proof claims. Render text safely and distinguish assumptions from tool evidence, including the footer.

Acceptance covers independent evidence on one target, a conformance-only neighbor with no proof, failed/empty attempts, atomic rejection, preservation across attribution calls and rejection of cross-kind stale inventories, full input binding including edits to an outside-scope driver, relocation/order stability, and inert hostile text. Legacy reports and successful legacy fingerprints remain compatible. Keep public explicit execution refused while adapters are absent.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0082, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161 and #234/#242's exact-target attribution contract (D-0163 as cited by #244). Update SPEC.md and README.md for this shipped evidence API and its execution limit; changed SPEC bullets cite their supporting decisions. The merger records the new evidence and assumption policy because the build cannot write decisions/. Keep ratified statements and locks unchanged.

issues.title: Discover Python components with stable source identities
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Extend project.ResolveComponents and manifest validation to explicit Python scopes for #244, preserving the existing Go and omitted-components legacy paths. Inventory each declared scope directory nonrecursively, including every non-test Python source file, files with no functions, and named functions and qualified methods whether selected or not. Use syntax-aware discovery without importing or executing inspected code. Include async definitions and class-qualified methods; distinguish nested named declarations and repeated definitions rather than silently collapsing them. Comments and strings containing apparent declarations create no components.

Python IDs combine language, project-relative module, qualified symbol and source, with deterministic ordinals where needed. Derive modules from source paths, keeping __init__ files distinct; host import paths, checkout location, line numbers and bodies cannot affect IDs. As in Go, reordering repeated declarations can change which declaration an ordinal selects. Hash complete source files and the exact supported inline Nagini contract bytes independently; ordinary comments and a # +nagini marker alone do not constitute a contract. Document the supported declaration and contract forms.

Resolve target, proof-contract, test and conformance references exactly once, using language-appropriate test files and contract syntax. Keep targets/contracts in scope and permit test/driver associations elsewhere inside the project with the separate input provenance used by component evidence. Reject malformed source, duplicate/ambiguous or missing selections, unsupported selected forms, non-clean paths and paths escaping through symlinks. Inventories remain sorted intent with no assurance. Keep Python execution guarded; never fall through to legacy verification.

Acceptance covers same-named methods in different classes/modules, async and nested declarations, decorated definitions, duplicate-name handling, fake declarations in strings/comments, function-free files, path containment, invalid references and contracts, and stable IDs after relocation, configuration reordering and body/line edits while hashes change with source or contract bytes. Keep all Go identities unchanged.

Decisions: D-0023, D-0024, D-0031, D-0152, D-0158 and D-0122. Update SPEC.md and README.md to describe Python discovery and its current execution limit. The merger records the Python identity and contract-hashing rules and cites them in the SPEC; this build cannot write decisions/. Keep ratified statements and locks unchanged.

issues.title: Discover TypeScript components with stable source identities
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Extend project.ResolveComponents and manifest validation to explicit TypeScript scopes for #244, preserving Go/Python inventories and legacy manifests. Inventory each declared scope directory nonrecursively, including non-test implementation files with no functions and all named functions, named function-valued bindings and qualified class methods whether selected or not. Use syntax-aware parsing without executing or importing project code; comments, strings and type-only declarations must not invent executable components. Handle async functions, arrow bindings, nested named declarations, constructors, accessors, static/instance methods and overload signatures with documented qualification rules: signatures attach to their implementation rather than creating separately proved functions. An unsupported selected construct must fail clearly rather than resolve to another declaration.

IDs combine language, project-relative module, qualified symbol and source, disambiguating repeated names without checkout paths, line numbers or bodies. Hash complete implementation files and retain all unchecked neighbors. Resolve target, language-appropriate test and conformance references exactly once, recording association input snapshots separately where they lie outside production scope. Reject malformed source, ambiguous/duplicate or missing references and paths escaping the project, including symlink escapes. TypeScript has no proof path under D-0024: reject proof selections explicitly and never manufacture proof/contract evidence from types, comments or declarations.

Acceptance covers functions, arrows, same-named methods in different classes/modules, overload implementations, accessors, function-free files, fake source declarations, containment and validation failures. Verify that body edits and relocation preserve IDs while source hashes change, configuration ordering is canonical, and discovery conveys no assurance. Keep explicit execution guarded until its adapters are connected; never substitute legacy checks.

Decisions: D-0023, D-0024, D-0029, D-0030, D-0152, D-0158 and D-0122. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the discovery contract, no-TypeScript-proof limitation and current execution support. The merger records and cites the TypeScript identity rules because the plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Keep ratified statements and locks unchanged.

issues.title: Establish Go component proofs from real Gobra runs
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Add an explicit Go proof execution adapter using the existing pinned Gobra path for #244. internal/gobra currently discovers bare function names after a package run; that is insufficient to construct verify.ComponentProofResult. Snapshot and stage the actual input files, run the pinned verifier with overflow checking and the existing sandbox/timeout protections, then bind its successful result to exact source and receiver-qualified component IDs and the contracts genuinely checked. Derive coverage from submitted units and successful tool results, never bare names or configured intent.

Retain the existing verifier's file/package units and // +gobra convention. This issue does not introduce extraction, invented stubs or a new contract-composition proof rule. Plain neighboring files can remain ordinary Go. Only a configured target with its own qualifying result becomes proved; same-file neighbors and contract helpers remain unchecked. Reject unsupported proof/contract combinations, including incompatible cross-package selections, with a precise preflight diagnostic; never omit a selected contract silently.

Return source-bound attempted results for failures, missing/malformed success output, verifier exceptions, timeout and cancellation, with diagnostics and no proof claim. Results identify the verifier pin and all actual input snapshots, including support files/dependencies that affect the run. Preserve evidence validation/immutability and keep the public gate guard.

Acceptance includes an integration test against pinned Gobra for a mixed ordinary Go package with one selected annotated function, an unselected same-file function and a plain-file neighbor; only the selected target is proved. Cover same-named methods/packages, skipped verifier files, unsubmitted or uncovered contracts, changed input bytes, nonzero exit and empty output. Deterministic process-boundary tests cover timeout/cancellation and cleanup without waiting for the real timeout. Legacy Gobra verification stays compatible.

Decisions: D-0003, D-0013, D-0016, D-0020, D-0111, D-0144, D-0148, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161 and #234/#242's attribution contract. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the actual adapter capability and remaining gate limit, citing support under D-0122. The merger records the exact-input execution policy; no decisions/, ratified statements or locks are changed by this build.

issues.title: Establish Python component proofs from real Nagini runs
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Add the Python component proof adapter for #244 using the Python inventory and exact-input evidence contract now available. Reuse the pinned Nagini recipe and # +nagini file convention. Stage immutable source inputs, run the actual verifier, and construct ComponentProofResult only from successful checks of the exact submitted declarations and selected contracts. Use canonical Python identities for explicit attribution; preserve legacy verification.

Proof remains limited to Nagini-supported marked source units. Ordinary Python neighbors and contract helpers retain unchecked proof status unless they have their own configured successful target result. Reject selected signatures/contracts or file combinations the adapter cannot genuinely check before running tools; no inferred proof from source discovery, marker presence, an unrelated file's success or a merely declared assumption. TypeScript still has no proof path. Record every actual input snapshot and pinned recipe in evidence. Failures, incomplete output, timeout and cancellation retain diagnostics without proof; preserve independent successes. Run in the existing isolated, network-free environment with bounded execution and cleanup.

Acceptance includes a real pinned Nagini run with one selected supported target and unselected neighbors, an invalid contract/body that fails, qualified duplicate short names, and selection of an unmarked/unsubmitted unit. Deterministic process-boundary tests cover empty success output, timeout, cancellation, changed inputs and cleanup. Keep public explicit execution blocked until the full gate path is connected.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0031, D-0032, D-0111, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161 and #234/#242's attribution contract. Update SPEC.md and README.md for this adapter and its actual limits under D-0122. The merger records the Python execution-attribution policy and cites it; the build cannot write decisions/ and must keep ratified statements and locks unchanged.

issues.title: Run selected component tests and conformance checks
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Implement actual runtime and conformance execution for explicit Go, Python and TypeScript selections in #244, using their inventories and separate evidence records. Document executable invocation signatures for source/symbol references; reject unsupported selections in preflight. Reuse the existing pinned language sandboxes, trace formats, conformance checker and gate-owned exploration harnesses. Runtime checks here are selected tests and assertions exercised by those runs, not production instrumentation.

Execute each selected test against the staged real project code and attribute its observed runner outcome to its exact check ID and configured targets. An exit code alone is insufficient when no selected test ran: zero matched, skipped-only, missing or incomplete test results establish no success. Other tests cannot satisfy selections; a pass does not imply complete target coverage. Preserve failed/timed-out attempts and diagnostics. Do not rewrite source implementations to make checks pass.

Invoke selected conformance drivers on the staged code and check their actual traces against the unchanged ratified model and bounds with TLC. Record sampled runs separately from exhaustive checks within bounds, including seed/parameters, counts, input snapshots and attempt coverage. Record the driver-to-target association as declared intent: passing traces alone do not demonstrate execution of every associated target/path. Preserve existing checked-code import enforcement where applicable. A model run without code traces establishes no conformance. An every-state claim requires the existing positive matching state counts, successful exhaustive run and no failed attempt check; sampled traces or incomplete/empty output cannot earn it. Keep conformance separate from proof, runtime and assumptions. Fingerprint selected tests/drivers, other executed inputs, model/bounds and tool pins, including out-of-scope helpers.

Acceptance exercises selected Go/Python/TypeScript tests and both sampled and exhaustive driver paths, wrong or zero matched tests, failing assertions, invalid traces, failed attempt coverage, timeout/cancellation and unsupported invocation rejection. Verify independent conformance/runtime/proof facts on the same target and no inherited evidence for neighbors or target-coverage claim from an unrelated driver. Use pinned-tool integration coverage and deterministic negative cases. Keep the public gate guard; finish and test adapters in this change.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0030, D-0043, D-0082, D-0086, D-0088, D-0090, D-0111, D-0152, D-0158 and D-0161. Update SPEC.md and README.md for supported selectors, invocation contracts and evidence limits under D-0122. The merger records the new invocation and runtime-attribution policy; no build edits decisions/, ratified statements or locks.

issues.title: Connect the explicit component gate and remove its blanket refusal
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Connect the component inventory, proof adapters and selected runtime/conformance adapters to verify.Check, verify.Run and the CLI for #244, then remove verify.ErrComponents and the blanket explicit-mode rejection. Run selected checks on one consistent staged snapshot and emit full JSON/Markdown receipts, including inventory-only scopes and unchecked neighbors. Validate the whole execution plan before tools start; unsupported language/check combinations receive precise errors. Never fall through to legacy execution or ignore selected checks.

Keep all existing ratification, pinned-statement, model, witness and known-bug checks. The explicit code path builds the applicable ordinary code and requires every selected executable proof/test/conformance check to succeed. It must not require an unselected Init/State/Successors/Try explorer or claim implicit model agreement. An unselected component is unchecked and does not itself fail the gate; declared assumptions do not satisfy executable checks. A selected missing, skipped, failed, cancelled or timed-out check fails the gate. Keep individual evidence independent of the gate result, preserving successful completed target checks when another fails. Once attempts have begun, failures must produce a failed report with their evidence/diagnostics, rather than discarding it or publishing an empty success.

Replace obsolete refusal assertions with execution/preflight tests; preserve unrelated acceptance guarantees. Omitted-components legacy behavior, successful receipts/fingerprints and gate outcomes remain compatible. RunModel starts no code tools. Ratified statements/locks remain unchanged.

Acceptance runs a real mixed Go package end to end through verify.Run and receipt output: one configured function proved, same-file and ordinary-file neighbors unchecked, independent selected tests/conformance visible, no project-wide proof claim. Failure and deterministic timeout cases leave the affected target unchecked with a failed receipt while preserving completed evidence. Cover Go and Python proof paths, TypeScript conformance/runtime-only support, inventory-only scopes, no implicit explorer requirement, zero matched checks, unsupported selections rejected before tool startup, fingerprint/input binding and legacy/model-only regressions. Run go test ./... and the relevant pinned-tool integration suite.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0031, D-0111, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161 and #234/#242's attribution contract. Update SPEC.md and README.md in this change to replace API-only and explicit-execution-unavailable claims with the shipped behavior, accurate examples and support limits; changed SPEC bullets cite the decisions. Under D-0122 the merger records the explicit gate policy and retirement of the D-0158 guard because the build cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Show every component's separate assurance in the dashboard
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish #244 by carrying explicit component inventory and evidence from receipts through internal/dashboard's snapshot/Project representation into the served UI. Cards and the project table must offer a component view keyed by repository and project, not only by shared model identity: two projects checking the same model can have different component evidence. List every scoped declaration and show its exact identity, source/contract hashes, selected checks and outcomes. Keep proof, bounded or sampled conformance with its actual bounds/counts, executed runtime checks, and explicitly unverified trusted assumptions separate. Show unchecked neighbors and failed/timed-out attempts clearly. Do not collapse these facts into one score or promote a partial proof to a project-wide guarantee.

Derive displayed proof and coverage counts from qualifying evidence, including when older reports carry stale top-level labels. Show gate pass/fail independently from successful component evidence; preserve the existing legacy assurance rules and model-only presentation. Cards/table summaries show component evidence and reachable details without blanket proof or unchecked labels. Totals count qualifying proved targets once, excluding contract helpers. Handle empty inventories and absent optional fields safely. Treat all source-derived identities, assumptions and diagnostics as text, with no executable HTML or Markdown injection.

Acceptance checks snapshot/API data and the rendered card, table and detail paths for a mixed receipt: one proved target, unchecked same-named neighbors, a contract-only helper, successful conformance with no proof, runtime results, a declared assumption, and a failed/timed-out proof alongside a failed gate. Verify two projects sharing one model remain separate, legacy reports retain their claims, empty inventories are handled, malicious strings stay inert and aggregate proof counts agree with target evidence. Exercise the data-to-view behavior, not only source-string presence.

Update SPEC.md and README.md for the component views and final supported workflow under D-0122. Audit all component-related documentation, including the principle and status sections, removing completed #224/API-only/Go-only/guard TODOs while accurately documenting remaining verifier restrictions and later #210 work. Confirm mixed-Go, failed-proof, separate-conformance and stable Python/TypeScript identity acceptance passes, completing every #244 requirement. Keep ratified statements/locks unchanged.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0070, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161, D-0162 and #234/#242's attribution contract. Changed SPEC bullets cite their support. The merger records any new display policy and reconciles the D-0163 record cited by #244; the plumbing build cannot write decisions/. #244 is complete for its parent only when the factory posts completion for this ratified plan's hash.
